title: Grief and Comfort
definition: Grief and comfort is the biblical reality that sorrow is real, but God draws near to the brokenhearted and gives hope through Christ.
summary: God comforts His people in grief without denying the reality of sorrow.
christFocus: Jesus wept, suffered, conquered death, and comforts His people with resurrection hope.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Grief is not a lack of faith. Scripture gives room for lament, tears, sorrow, and honest pain before God. The Lord is near to the brokenhearted.

God's comfort does not minimize loss. He comforts through His presence, promises, people, Word, and the hope of resurrection. Jesus Himself wept at the tomb of Lazarus, showing compassion in the face of death.

For believers, grief is real but not hopeless. Christ has conquered death, and God will one day wipe away every tear.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Many grieving people feel pressure to move on quickly or pretend they are fine. Grief and comfort matters because it gives permission to mourn while anchoring sorrow in the hope of Christ.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Bring grief honestly to God. Receive comfort through Scripture, prayer, and the body of Christ. Comfort others gently without rushing their sorrow or offering shallow answers.
